stories.summary: Ketogenic diets have attracted enormous attention for their purported health benefits, particularly their ability to promote weight loss. stories.title: Blocking receptor signals can help treat fibrosis

stories.title: Genetics can make a 10-year difference in the onset of Alzheimer's disease

stories.title: Smart footwear turns ordinary steps into checks of blood flow to feet

stories.title: Exercise may be good for your social life, studies in mice suggest
stories.summary: If you've been thinking about joining one of the social running, walking or hiking clubs popping up on your social media feeds, new research from The Ohio State University offers another reason to give it a try: Working out with other people might serve as a social lubricant.

stories.title: Sugar made by gut bacterium may help the body burn visceral fat
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that a sugar produced by a gut bacterium can increase energy burning in visceral fat—the harmful fat that accumulates around internal organs—while reducing weight gain and improving metabolic health, offering a potential new approach to tackling obesity.

stories.title: Neurosteroid offers clues to brain changes linked to depression
stories.summary: UT Southwestern Medical Center researchers and colleagues, including two at UT Dallas, have found evidence that pregnenolone—a naturally occurring steroid hormone the body produces from cholesterol—may alter patterns of communication between key brain regions involved in depression and cognitive…

stories.title: Why don't weight-loss drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy work for everyone?
stories.summary: Why do Ozempic and Wegovy produce dramatic weight loss for some people but disappointing results for others? stories.title: New evidence questions benefits of turmeric for knee arthritis
stories.summary: A new Cochrane review has found that turmeric supplements may provide little or no clinically important pain relief for people with knee osteoarthritis, challenging conclusions from earlier research that suggested a benefit. stories.title: Turmeric supplements offer little benefit for knee osteoarthritis

stories.title: FDA approves drug for infantile-onset Niemann-Pick type C after analysis finds longer survival
stories.summary: Researchers at the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and their collaborators at Beren Therapeutics, Thousand Oaks, California, have developed a treatment for infants with Niemann-Pick type C (NPC) disease, which is a rare and rapidly fatal pediatric neurodegenerative disorder.

stories.title: Targeting immune overactivity in Down syndrome shows promise in phase 2 clinical trial

stories.summary: Even when 24-hour circadian rhythms persist into old age, faster multi-hour "ultradian" rhythms weaken significantly. stories.summary: Parkinson's disease is a progressive brain disorder that damages dopamine-producing neurons, causing symptoms to worsen over time. The disease is associated with motor difficulties that can manifest as tremors, stiffness, poor balance and slow movements.

stories.title: Could brain energy mismatches explain altered experiences in schizophrenia?
stories.summary: A minute can seem shorter when you are having fun, yet it feels painfully long when you're bored or stressed. Although this gap between actual time and perceived time is something we all experience, it can be much more pronounced in people with schizophrenia-spectrum conditions.

stories.title: A simple supplement could help your immune system fight cancer and viral infections
stories.summary: A surprising discovery from Rockefeller University suggests that a common amino acid could play a powerful role in protecting against cancer and viral infections.

stories.title: Brain–heart interactions may predict recovery from oxygen loss
stories.summary: Low oxygen levels in the brain, or cerebral anoxia, are a leading cause of death worldwide. Patients who recover from cerebral anoxia deal with persistent neurological issues that worsen their quality of life.

stories.title: Alzheimer’s may start shrinking two brain regions years before memory loss
stories.summary: Johns Hopkins scientists have uncovered hidden warning signs of Alzheimer’s disease that may appear up to a decade before memory loss begins.

stories.title: Using AI to accelerate neuroscience research
stories.summary: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into neuroscience is changing how scientists engage with data, improving our understanding of the brain and leading to better ways of training computational models.

stories.title: New biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease, depression and beyond
stories.summary: Newly developed biomarkers may enhance clinicians' ability to detect and treat disorders of the nervous system, including Alzheimer's disease, mood disorders and neurodevelopmental conditions. The findings were presented at Neuroscience 2026, the annual meeting of the Society for Neuroscience.

stories.title: Sex differences in pain, inflammation and Alzheimer's disease
stories.summary: New evidence supports the idea that differences within and between sexes impact how neurological disorders progress and respond to treatment. The findings were presented at Neuroscience 2026, the annual meeting of the Society for Neuroscience.

stories.title: Brain-computer interfaces: A new voice for people with paralysis
stories.summary: Recent advancements in brain-computer interfaces are helping restore communication in clinical trial participants who have lost the ability to speak or make voluntary movements. New findings were presented at Neuroscience 2026, the annual meeting of the Society for Neuroscience.

stories.title: New brain-body connections expand understanding of Alzheimer's disease
stories.summary: Research on Alzheimer's disease (AD) and aging has found strong connections between physical health and brain health. These new connections were presented at Neuroscience 2026, the annual meeting of the Society for Neuroscience.

stories.title: Predator-like scent activates an anxiety-related brain circuit in mice
stories.summary: Anxiety disorders are some of the most common psychiatric conditions, estimated to affect around 4.4% of people worldwide, according to the World Health Organization. While neuroscientists have been studying these disorders for decades, their neural underpinnings are not yet fully understood.

stories.title: Scientists find a simple daily routine linked to less pain and depression
stories.summary: A simple change to your daily routine could make a surprising difference in how you feel, both physically and mentally. University of Missouri researchers found that older adults who followed consistent daily schedules reported less physical pain and fewer symptoms of depression, even when they…

stories.title: A new fiber supplement could help millions suffering from irritable bowel syndrome
stories.summary: Scientists have developed a promising new fiber supplement that improves gut health in people with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) without worsening bloating, pain, or other digestive symptoms.

stories.title: Stanford scientists discover hidden brain signals that predict Alzheimer’s years before symptoms
stories.summary: Stanford researchers have discovered that hidden patterns of brain activity can predict Alzheimer’s risk years before memory problems appear, potentially offering an earlier warning than traditional biomarkers.

stories.title: Exercise after ACL surgery may protect knees from early osteoarthritis
stories.summary: A new study suggests that the right kind of exercise could help protect young adults from early knee osteoarthritis following ACL surgery. Researchers found that a four-month supervised rehabilitation program improved pain, muscle strength, and quality of life without damaging knee cartilage.

stories.title: Preliminary study finds a clue in the quest to help diagnose CTE in the living
stories.summary: Scientists stumbled onto a hint that measuring a toxic protein tied to Alzheimer's disease just might one day be useful in diagnosing a different brain disease in football players and others who have suffered repeated blows to the head.

stories.title: Why a Little Extra Weight May Benefit Older People
stories.summary: Even in the age of obesity drugs, researchers say many don’t need to shed pounds.

stories.title: Yale scientists reveal what really slows aging and what doesn't
stories.summary: Yale researchers have discovered that certain prescription drugs, healthy diets, and exercise can measurably slow biological aging, while popular anti-aging supplements appear largely ineffective.

stories.title: Researchers trial AI coach for diabetes
stories.summary: For many people with type 2 diabetes, the challenge isn't understanding what they need to do to stay well. It's doing it consistently. Managing the condition often requires a long-term commitment to healthier eating patterns, regular exercise and medication.

stories.summary: It is generally safe for older adults without a history of cardiovascular disease to discontinue statins for primary prevention, according to a study published online Nov.

stories.title: RNA switch lets drugs control gene therapy protein production
stories.summary: Bioengineers at the University of California San Diego have developed a technology that allows drugs to control when cells produce therapeutic proteins, which could potentially make gene therapies safer and more adaptable for treating chronic diseases.

stories.title: Genetic Switch Helped Evolve the Large Primate Brain
stories.summary: How did the human brain evolve to be so large and complex? Researchers discovered a primate-specific DNA regulatory switch controlling the shared DACH1 gene, boosting specialized basal radial glia stem cells that build the cerebral cortex without needing new genes.

stories.title: GLP-1s often contain untested additive combinations, study finds
stories.summary: Use of GLP-1 receptor agonist medications (GLP-1s) has skyrocketed in recent years, and many people are using "compounded" GLP-1 products: medicines that include GLP-1s as well as other active substances, some of which are not regulated by the FDA.

stories.title: New body map traces origins of complex movements in the brains of mice
stories.summary: A new biological blueprint of how the body of a mouse is represented in its brain could help scientists answer a fundamental question: How do we perform complex motions that use more than one body part, such as coordinating arm, hand, head and lips to sip a spoonful of soup?

stories.title: CRISPR Enhancer Editing Rescues Autism Brain Organoids
stories.summary: Rather than cutting DNA, scientists used precision CRISPR activation aimed at natural gene "dials" to boost healthy copies of CHD8 and SCN2A in human brain organoids, restoring normal tissue growth and neuronal firing exclusively in mutated cells.

stories.title: A microbe-made molecule may reverse gut damage by boosting NAD levels
stories.summary: Scientists at Rutgers Health have discovered a molecule produced by "good" gut bacteria that rapidly heals the intestinal lining, protecting against severe inflammatory diseases and triggering increased production of a coenzyme whose levels diminish with age.

stories.title: Blood NAD levels track heart disease, not aging, study of more than 1,000 adults finds
stories.summary: Vilnius University researchers find that whole-blood NAD levels remain stable with age in healthy men and increase slightly in women, but are lower in people with cardiovascular disease, particularly hypertension.

stories.title: Some ketogenic diets found to cause mitochondrial stress and lead to inflammation
stories.summary: New University of Cincinnati Cancer Center research found that a ketogenic diet high in long-chain saturated fatty acids can increase inflammation.

stories.title: Mapping the Brain’s Energy Budget: How ATP Fuels Thought
stories.summary: How much energy does a single thought cost? The study will map the brain's metabolic budget across scales, solving why active neurons burn sugar rapidly and how brain cells survive oxygen loss.

stories.title: Hidden Body Map in Brain Explains Complex Coordination
stories.summary: How do you effortlessly coordinate your hand, arm, head, and lips to sip soup? Columbia neuroscientists discovered a previously hidden full-body map inside the brain's secondary motor cortex (M2), found within its resting-state neural chatter, that orchestrates complex multi-limb actions.

stories.title: Irregular Sleep Schedules Tied to Depression & Loneliness
stories.summary: When you sleep matters just as much as how long you sleep. Analyzing five months of smart-ring data from 23,000 adults, researchers found that irregular daily sleep-wake schedules weaken circadian alignment and correspond with severe depression, anxiety, and loneliness.

stories.title: Brain atlas reveals how aging unfolds differently across brain regions, cell types and sexes
stories.summary: How do we age, and how do we become more at risk of brain diseases as we age? An Arizona State University-led team is helping answer those questions with a new high-resolution atlas of the aging primate brain.

stories.title: Waves that clear waste from the brain during sleep are impaired in older adults
stories.summary: As people age, they may sleep for shorter periods and wake up more frequently during the night. In addition to those disruptions, MIT researchers have now discovered that a process responsible for flushing waste from the brain during sleep is commonly impaired in older people.

stories.title: Hamster hibernation study offers clues to Alzheimer's disease
stories.summary: Researchers at VIB and KU Leuven have discovered that hibernation triggers changes in brain cells that partially resemble those in Alzheimer's disease.

stories.title: Vitamin D may help control lung inflammation during flu infection, study in mice suggests
stories.summary: Vitamin D may help the body fight influenza by controlling inflammation and the amount of virus in the lungs, according to a study in mice led by researchers at Penn State.

stories.title: AI analysis of heart ultrasounds may help flag long-term cardiovascular or dementia-related death risk
stories.summary: Having a heart age older than one's actual age, as estimated using artificial intelligence (AI) analysis of ultrasound images, was associated with worse outcomes, according to results presented today at the ESC Digital & AI Summit 2026.

stories.title: Does a heart stent prevent future heart attacks in stable patients? 25-year follow-up offers new insight
stories.summary: When doctors find a blockage in a patient's heart arteries, a common treatment option is a procedure to open the artery and restore blood flow. But does getting a stent actually help prevent a future heart attack or help someone live longer?

stories.title: Study of 750,000 pregnancies reveals a surprising twist about Ozempic and Wegovy
stories.summary: A study of more than 750,000 pregnancies found that early exposure to Ozempic, Wegovy, and similar drugs was not linked to increased pregnancy complications when used for weight loss, but was associated with a higher risk of premature birth when prescribed for diabetes.

stories.title: Stopping statins after 70 may be safer than expected, but there's a catch
stories.summary: A major study of nearly 1,900 older adults suggests that stopping statins after age 70 may be relatively safe in the short term for people who have never experienced a heart attack or stroke.

stories.title: Taking a closer look at stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation
stories.summary: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), one of the most common heart rhythm disorders, are at increased risk of ischemic stroke, a stroke caused by a blood clot blocking blood flow to the brain, as well as blood clots that can travel to other parts of the body.

stories.title: China approves first oral GLP-1 weight-loss pill
stories.summary: China has approved its first orally administered GLP-1 weight-loss drug, permitting Eli Lilly to sell its orforglipron pill in a market where 630 million adults could be overweight or obese by 2050.

stories.title: ‘Never thought I’d eat that’: how vegetable prescriptions are helping Britons with diabetes
stories.summary: WellFed participants in Cornwall report better blood sugar levels with help of free veg boxes, cooking and gardening The participants admitted that throughout their life, their food choices had been far from ideal: egg and chips, hearty roasts, raw fry – a Cornish one-pan dish of bacon, potatoes…

stories.title: What is 'food is medicine'? Two experts explain this decades‑old approach to health care that is taking on new life
stories.summary: Mountains of scientific evidence support both the negative and positive effects of our eating habits on our health. Research shows that a healthy diet can help those suffering from chronic health conditions like type 2 diabetes, heart disease and high blood pressure.

stories.title: Without this protein, damaged muscle fills with fat and scar tissue
stories.summary: Researchers have uncovered a surprising hidden function of a protein that may hold the key to repairing damaged muscles and treating muscular dystrophy. Known for protecting chromosomes, TRF2 also helps muscle stem cells maintain their identity and regenerate injured tissue.

stories.title: Molecular mapping of 8 million cells brings cerebral architecture into focus
stories.summary: University of California, Irvine researchers have mapped approximately 8 million cells in regions deep within the human brain, identifying 60 distinct types and revealing how they form cellular communities.

stories.title: Animal vs. plant protein reveals a surprising testosterone divide
stories.summary: A surprising new study suggests that where men get their protein may be linked to their testosterone levels. stories.title: Key brain area reveals distinct zones whose boundaries blur with age
stories.summary: Scientists in the Center for Human Brain Variation at the Broad Institute have charted previously hidden architecture and patterns of cellular makeup in a key part of the brain called the striatum, which is involved in decision-making and movement and is affected in psychiatric disorders, addiction…

stories.title: 3D Genome Atlas Reveals Early Roots of Schizophrenia
stories.summary: How does the human brain wire its reward and motor centers before birth? stories.summary: Does Alzheimer's start outside the brain? Gladstone Institutes researchers mapped the first atlas of 92 blood proteins that cross the blood-brain barrier, discovering that the barrier shuts down the import of protective liver proteins before it ever begins leaking toxins.

stories.title: How to test whether brain organoids possess consciousness
stories.summary: The development of brain organoids is advancing at a breakneck pace. Researchers are creating tiny cell clusters in the lab that behave like fragments of the human brain. Whether such organoids could develop intelligence—or even consciousness—remains a matter of debate.

stories.title: First human model for form of inherited heart disease uses realistic levels of mutant protein
stories.summary: Inherited cardiomyopathies—diseases of the heart muscle, which cause the heart to have a harder time pumping blood to the rest of the body—are the leading cause of heart failure in young adults.

stories.title: Inflammation is involved in the earliest stages of atherosclerosis
stories.summary: Inflammation plays an important role in the development of atherosclerosis from its earliest stages, long before the onset of symptoms or cardiovascular events such as heart attack or stroke.

stories.title: Blood thinner could offer a new way to treat osteoarthritis
stories.summary: Osteoarthritis is the most common form of joint disease, a condition that causes joints to become painful and stiff. It can happen to any joint when the cartilage cushioning the ends of bones breaks down or wears away. Currently, there are no approved drugs to slow or stop the underlying disease.

stories.title: Pink noise played during sleep shows promise for Alzheimer’s memory loss

stories.summary: Aging is about far more than wrinkles and gray hair, despite what social media and advertisements might have us believe. The real concern lies beneath the surface, where the biology of aging is intertwined with a host of diseases, from heart disease to neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's…

stories.title: New atlas traces how key human brain cells develop before and after birth
stories.summary: Scientists have long known that many developing brain cells originate in one region and migrate to another as they mature.

stories.title: Mapping the marmoset's deep-brain cell diversity and building a tool to integrate data across species
stories.summary: Researchers have built a high-resolution brain-cell atlas that could do for neuroscience what the Human Genome Project did for genetics.

stories.title: Researchers pioneer new technology to track brain tissue from laboratory to data
stories.summary: Scientists studying the human brain have long faced a complex obstacle: because of the scarcity of neurotypical human brain tissue, tissue samples from a single brain must be shared across research entities.

stories.title: Researchers play critical role in developing new atlas of brain cells
stories.summary: Capturing a complete picture of what causes brain diseases from schizophrenia and Parkinson's disease to addiction has long been a challenge for scientists.

stories.title: Cheap drug may prevent second stroke by lowering blood pressure
stories.summary: It's vital to lower blood pressure after a stroke, so the survivor doesn't suffer another as they recover. And it appears this safety measure can be achieved on the cheap, a new study says.

stories.title: Head-to-head trial reveals better immune-dampening drug for psoriatic arthritis
stories.summary: A newer immune-dampening drug appears to effectively quell pain and swelling in joints affected by psoriatic arthritis, a new study says.

stories.title: Food insecurity screen validated in young families may not fit older adults
stories.summary: The U.S. population age 80 and older is projected to double over the next two decades, yet few of the tools health systems use to screen for food insecurity, transportation barriers and other social needs have been validated in older adults.

stories.title: Reddit mental health advice comes with a warning
stories.summary: People seeking advice about depression and anxiety from community-based Reddit groups are often encouraged to get professional help, but a new Flinders University study has found that some responses to people in crisis lack clear next steps or the urgency recommended by clinical guidelines.

stories.title: Crows can make decisions twice as fast as humans, scientists discover
stories.summary: Crows may be even smarter than we thought, and their brains are astonishingly fast. Researchers at the University of Tübingen discovered that crows can make visual decisions twice as quickly as humans and monkeys, taking just 235 milliseconds on average to identify the direction of moving dots…

stories.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
stories.summary: Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant.

stories.title: Could an erratic sleep schedule be harming your mental health?
stories.summary: People with irregular sleep-wake schedules may experience more severe symptoms of anxiety, depression and even loneliness, according to a large study led by UC San Francisco and UC San Diego.

stories.title: How long does menopause last? By one measure, the rest of your life
stories.summary: Women who've had menopausal symptoms for years—such as night sweats, mood changes and new aches and pains—might be wondering when they will ever end.

stories.title: Christchurch mutation points to potential gene therapy avenue for Parkinson's
stories.summary: A rare genetic mutation may protect against developing Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementia, a new study from researchers at Oregon Health & Science University suggests.

stories.title: Are max strength cold and flu pills worth the money?
stories.summary: Some cold and flu remedies cost 20 times as much as a basic pack of paracetamol or ibuprofen.

stories.title: Walking and weight training may not be enough to keep your bones strong
stories.summary: A surprising new study suggests that walking, jogging, and even traditional weight training may be less effective at stimulating bone formation than high-intensity sports involving explosive movements and sudden changes in direction.

stories.title: 'Living medicine' tackles drug-resistant biofilms growing on ventilation tubes
stories.summary: A "living medicine" has thinned biofilms of antibiotic-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa in the lungs of pigs, according to the findings of a study published in the journal eBioMedicine.

stories.title: Pausing blood pressure meds on day of surgery benefits older adults
stories.summary: Pausing a patient's usual dose of blood pressure medication on the day of surgery reduces the rate of very low blood pressure requiring treatment during the operation compared with taking their medication as normal, finds a trial of older adults, published by The BMJ.

stories.title: Experts urge caution over drug company campaigns to destigmatize obesity
stories.summary: We should be wary of campaigns by pharmaceutical companies to destigmatize obesity, say experts in The BMJ. stories.title: Ballet dancers show distinct brain responses to other people's facial emotions
stories.summary: Dance training can influence how we perceive not only movement but also everyday emotional expressions, according to new research from the Centre for Cognition and Neuroscience at City St George's, University of London.

stories.title: Free SAD lamps given out as disorder 'makes it hard to do anything on darker days'
stories.summary: Seasonal affective disorder can affect mood, energy and sleep during the winter months.

stories.title: Clinical trial explores potential brain health benefits of dietary supplement
stories.summary: A dietary supplement called urolithin A increased blood flow to the brain during mental activity in middle-aged adults with obesity, according to a University of Oklahoma study published in JAMA Network Open.

stories.title: AI-powered imaging tracks thousands of brain cancer cells moving through living tissue
stories.summary: By combining live imaging of brain tissue with artificial intelligence, researchers at Uppsala University have developed a method that reveals how individual glioblastoma cells spread through the brain, how they can switch between different ways of moving and how they are affected by cancer…

stories.title: Jessica Chastain to Star in New Broadway Play ‘Lost Lear’
stories.summary: Chastain will portray an actress with dementia whose most vivid memories are of rehearsing for the title role in “King Lear.”

stories.title: New clinical definition of obesity could help target care more effectively, saving time and money
stories.summary: The traditional way of assessing whether someone is overweight using body mass index (BMI) may fail to capture whether excess body fat is harmful and could be supplemented with a second measure when assessing patients, a new UCL study suggests.

stories.title: All of Us study finds thousands of new genetic variants affecting drug responses
stories.summary: A study of nearly 100,000 diverse Americans identified thousands of new variants in genes that influence our responses to prescription drugs

stories.title: Low-cost parenting app reduces sexual violence against adolescent girls by more than half, study finds
stories.summary: A digital parenting program has reduced sexual violence and exploitation among adolescent girls in Tanzania by more than half, according to new research led by the University of Oxford's Department of Social Policy and Intervention.

stories.title: Brain Moves Its Touch Center to Keep Feeling Sensation
stories.summary: Why does artificial touch fade over time? Penn State engineers used fNIRS brain imaging to solve sensory habituation during transcutaneous nerve stimulation, discovering a 5-second pulse protocol that maintains a stable sense of touch while the brain recruits distributed networks.

stories.title: Why Nervous System Hyperarousal Keeps Jolting You Awake
stories.summary: Ever jolt awake with a racing heart just as you drift off? A study in PLOS Mental Health reveals that frequent hypnic jerks—or sleep starts—are not simple muscle twitches, but markers of anxiety, insomnia severity, and nervous system hyperarousal.

stories.title: Multiple Sclerosis Atrophy Spreads From High-Stress Neural Hubs
stories.summary: Why does brain volume loss in multiple sclerosis follow distinct patterns? An MRI study of 2,187 patients reveals that atrophy originates in metabolically exhausted network hubs—including the thalamus and sensorimotor cortices—spreading outward along structural connections.

stories.title: Daytime Sleep Waves in Parkinson’s Linked to Hallucinations
stories.summary: When sleep invades wakefulness: An EEG study of 84 Parkinson’s patients reveals that sleep-like slow brain waves intrude into daytime consciousness, directly tracking with hallucinations and cognitive decline while offering a potential prodromal biomarker.

stories.title: Psychedelic aftereffects may offer a window into psychotic symptoms
stories.summary: Every night, as he fell asleep, a 25-year-old man saw an eye in his ceiling. It was huge and unblinking, and it felt as if the whole world was being sucked into it. He didn't have psychosis, and he wasn't on drugs.

stories.title: Blood proteins reveal how menopause may shape brain health later
stories.summary: Researchers are uncovering the cascade of molecular events that happen when women undergo menopause.

stories.title: Jolting awake often associated with poorer sleep and higher anxiety, survey finds
stories.summary: People who frequently startle awake while falling asleep—a phenomenon researchers call "sleep starts" or hypnic jerks—report poorer sleep quality, greater insomnia severity and higher anxiety than those who do not, according to a new study published in PLOS Mental Health by Tanja Grünberger and…

stories.title: Blood-thinning drug limits cartilage damage and relieves osteoarthritis pain
stories.summary: A study in animals suggests a drug used to thin blood might eventually be able to slow down the development of osteoarthritis. Currently, there are no approved drugs capable of doing this

stories.title: Artificial light in your office may affect your health
stories.summary: Your office lights may be affecting more than your eyes—but a midday lunch walk can help.

stories.title: Regular coffee drinking appears to change how your gut works
stories.summary: If you drink coffee regularly, it appears to alter not only your gut bacteria but also the physiology of the gut itself.

stories.title: Sudden confusion in the hospital may signal higher dementia risk later in life
stories.summary: Hospitalized older adults can suddenly become disoriented and struggle to make sense of their surroundings. stories.title: Receptor map uncovers hidden sites that could guide asthma drug design
stories.summary: Researchers at the Center for Genomic Regulation (CRG) have developed a new way of identifying new druggable sites on a family of proteins that could help design treatments with fewer side effects for a very wide range of conditions from heart disease to depression.

stories.title: First atlas tracks proteins that cross the blood-brain barrier
stories.summary: Your brain is protected by the blood-brain barrier—a network of cells in the brain's blood vessels that serves as a border between the brain and the rest of your bloodstream.

stories.title: Lifetime trauma linked to dementia and memory problems in older Australians, study
stories.summary: The study of more than 1,800 older Australians found that people who had experienced lifetime trauma were more likely to have mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or dementia and performed worse on working memory and executive function tests.

stories.title: A gut microbe shields mice from Parkinson's-like brain damage
stories.summary: Parkinson's disease is usually thought of as a brain disease, but many patients notice gut trouble—constipation above all—years or even decades before their hands begin to tremble.

stories.title: Canine companionship, with a catch: Health effects of big-city dog ownership differ by location
stories.summary: How neighborhoods support healthy aging is a key question for aging societies. Yet little is known about how dog walking, an everyday activity, interacts with the neighborhood environment in dense Asian cities.

stories.title: Energy drinks linked to 11 times more reports of cardiac arrest
stories.summary: A new study found that energy drinks and stimulant supplements were linked to disproportionately frequent reports of serious heart problems, including 11 times more reports of cardiac arrest and 4.5 times more reports of heart attacks.

stories.title: Obesity linked to up to 27% lower risk of death in dementia
stories.summary: A surprising study of more than 4,500 older adults found that people who were overweight or obese when diagnosed with dementia had a 16% to 27% lower risk of death than those at a normal weight.

stories.title: Senior doctors call off two-day strike planned this month
stories.summary: Consultants in England were due to walk out on 25 November in disputes over pay and working conditions.

stories.title: Subtle Changes in Speech May Help Predict Dementia Risk

stories.title: Experiences reshape brain cell connections, synapse mapping reveals
stories.summary: Experiences and changes in the environment cause widespread alterations in connections between brain cells, influencing brain activity, research suggests.

stories.title: Could Your Voice Predict Your Dementia Risk?
stories.summary: Researchers are increasingly embracing what was once considered an intriguing but relatively fringe idea: that subtle changes in speech can help predict and track cognitive decline.

stories.title: Fewer than 5% of US military veterans may achieve optimal heart health

stories.summary: Fox Chase Cancer Center researchers identified a potential therapeutic target for pancreatic cancer after showing that tumor growth can be slowed and immune suppression can be reduced in preclinical trials by blocking a particular protein, called anoctamin 6 (ANO6).

stories.title: Scientists confirm fruit and vegetable skin really is good for you
stories.summary: Parts of plants that are usually wasted, from kiwi skin to squash seeds, contain more fibre than the parts of the plant we do eat

stories.title: Many women have never discussed heart health with a clinician, and most report multiple symptoms
stories.summary: Heart disease is the leading cause of death in women, and the risk rises during the menopause years. But an international study has revealed that only half of women know this. Many have never talked about their heart with a doctor or a nurse, and the majority are living with multiple symptoms.

stories.title: Cold Triggers a Hidden Molecular Pathway That Extends Lifespan, Study Finds
stories.summary: Can we harness this? ScienceAlert stories are written, fact-checked, and edited by humans, never generated by AI. Don't miss a story, subscribe here.

stories.title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say
stories.summary: Chomping on vegtable skins, seeds and stalks could give us vital fibre, say food scientists.

stories.title: Scientists discover why chronic back pain feels so personal
stories.summary: A surprising discovery at UC San Diego suggests that chronic lower back pain may become deeply embedded in the brain's sense of personal identity.

stories.title: The parts of fruits and vegetables most throw away could save your health—and the planet
stories.summary: Most of us routinely discard the peels, skins, stalks and seeds of fruits and vegetables at mealtime. But new research from King's College London suggests these scraps could be a valuable—and overlooked—source of dietary fiber, offering potential benefits for both public health and the environment.

stories.title: Manosphere and online misogyny should be treated as public health issues, say UK experts
stories.summary: Report calls for an effort to tackle harms in similar way to obesity and smoking, and stresses need to ‘offer boys something better’ The manosphere and online misogyny should be treated by the government as a public health issue, in the same way as obesity or smoking, experts have said.

stories.title: Could a few bad dietary choices worsen your next immune response?
stories.summary: Scientists have long known that diet shapes the immune system. Now, a UC San Francisco team has found that even a brief dietary change can substantially change how the body responds to skin irritation, at least in mice.

stories.title: When things go bump in the night: How our brains trick us into hearing things that aren't there
stories.summary: It's 3 a.m. You've woken from a dead sleep because you've heard a thud in the darkness or a floorboard creaking downstairs. Or perhaps you've woken because you have the unmistakable sensation you're not alone.

stories.title: Tumor mutations and immune activity may reveal who benefits from investigational lymphoma drug
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Tsukuba conducted a physician-initiated phase 2 clinical trial of dasatinib in patients with relapsed or refractory T-follicular helper cell lymphoma (TFHL), an aggressive and difficult-to-treat blood cancer.

stories.title: Heat waves and pollution increase stroke risk in older adults, study finds
stories.summary: A study conducted in Brazil by researchers at the University of São Paulo (USP) found that each additional day spent under a heat wave in São Paulo is associated with an increased risk of acute stroke in people ages 65 and older.

stories.title: New Transporter Bypasses Blood-Brain Barrier to Deliver Creatine
stories.summary: How can drugs bypass the brain's tightest security checkpoint? Researchers at the University of Eastern Finland discovered that hijacking the sodium-dependent multivitamin transporter (SMVT) allows creatine derivatives to cross the blood-brain barrier, offering hope for rare deficiency syndromes.

stories.title: Healthy diet may lower heart disease risk after cancer
stories.summary: Eating a healthy diet is associated with a reduced risk of heart disease and death among cancer survivors, according to a study published today in JACC: Advances.

stories.title: Antibody candidate could help preserve appetite and muscle strength in patients with cancer
stories.summary: In cancer cachexia, patients continue to lose weight, muscle and fat even when they eat. A KAIST research team has developed a therapeutic candidate that blocks a signal responsible for appetite suppression, weight loss and excessive energy expenditure.

stories.title: STI screening linked to fewer preterm births
stories.summary: Screening and treating pregnant patients for three common sexually transmitted infections (STIs) twice during pregnancy was associated with a 23% lower risk of preterm birth compared with standard care, according to a randomized clinical trial published in Clinical Infectious Diseases from…

stories.title: Vitamin-carrying protein pathway shows promise for brain drug delivery
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Eastern Finland have identified a transporter protein with the potential to open new avenues for improving creatine delivery into the brain and for developing other therapies targeting the central nervous system.

stories.title: These Patients Struggle With Runaway Bones. Finally There’s Hope.
stories.summary: F.O.P., a rare genetic condition, causes uncontrolled explosions of bone. A new drug may slow or halt the process.

stories.title: A single brain signal may explain schizophrenia's most puzzling symptoms
stories.summary: Scientists have identified a weakened brain signal that may connect several seemingly unrelated symptoms of schizophrenia, including sensory processing difficulties, disorganized speech, and greater symptom severity.

stories.title: Six popular sugar substitutes linked to faster brain aging
stories.summary: A study of nearly 13,000 adults found that people consuming the most artificial sweeteners experienced a 62% faster decline in memory and thinking skills, equivalent to approximately 1.6 additional years of brain aging.

stories.title: STAT+: Pharmalittle: We’re reading about a new policy for compounding peptides, a PBM disclosure rule, and more
stories.summary: HHS released a policy that will temporarily allow compounding pharmacies to manufacture some peptide products

stories.title: Less than 42 minutes of bright daylight linked to higher dementia risk
stories.summary: Getting more daylight could be linked to a surprisingly powerful benefit for brain health. In a study of more than 87,000 adults, researchers found that higher daytime light exposure was associated with a 16% lower risk of dementia, with longer exposure to bright light linked to even greater…

stories.title: New blood test can detect changes associated with Alzheimer's disease
stories.summary: Brain changes associated with Alzheimer's disease can be detected by a new type of blood test -- and a growing number of patients are asking their doctors about it.

stories.title: NHS Western Isles prescribing weight loss drugs at triple the rate of other health boards
stories.summary: A new report finds "significant variation" between Scotland's health boards prescribing new medicines.

stories.title: Your blood pressure could be dangerous even when your numbers look normal
stories.summary: Researchers have discovered a small group of brain cells that prevents dangerous blood pressure swings, even when average readings appear normal. The finding reveals a hidden source of cardiovascular risk and could open the door to new treatments that protect the heart and brain.

stories.title: Red meat nutrient may amp up inflammation
stories.summary: A nutrient abundant in red meat and commonly used in exercise supplements may amplify inflammation.

stories.title: Breathing “Thin Air” May Protect Against Parkinson’s
stories.summary: Can breathing thin mountain air help Parkinson's patients? Researchers demonstrated that 39 minutes of controlled intermittent hypoxia safely lowers stress hormones, raises anti-inflammatory adiponectin, and protects BDNF levels without disturbing sleep.

stories.title: Brain Disease Is Pervasive in N.F.L., New Estimate Suggests
stories.summary: Using statistical techniques, a new study has arrived at a harrowing estimate: Three of four retired pro football players most likely had C.T.E. at death.

stories.title: STAT+: Pharmalittle: We’re reading about 340B battles, new results for a Lilly weight loss drug, and more
stories.summary: Missouri attorney general warned Eli Lilly to discontinue requiring hospitals to provide claims data to receive discounted medicines under 340B program

stories.title: STAT+: Lilly’s triple-G drug beats Ozempic in head-to-head study
stories.summary: Eli Lilly announced that its investigational drug retatrutide was more effective at lowering blood sugar and cutting weight than Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic in a large diabetes study.

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden reason why muscles weaken with age
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden defense mechanism in aging muscles that sacrifices strength to protect cells from damage.

stories.title: ‘Ferritin face’: are social media claims about iron deficiency fact – or fiction?
stories.summary: Experts say symptoms such as dark circles under the eyes, grey skin, cracked lips and hair loss can be a warning sign – but there are other factors too TikTok is rife with influencers warning of “ferritin face”, a term they use to describe the pallor, dark circles, dry skin, and hair loss claimed…

stories.title: A simple daily fiber supplement reduced arthritis pain and improved strength
stories.summary: A new clinical trial suggests that a simple daily fiber supplement could significantly reduce knee osteoarthritis pain, improve muscle strength, and make the body less sensitive to pain.

stories.title: Finding the Brain’s Mood Switch in Bipolar Disorder
stories.summary: What causes the sudden transition between depression and mania in bipolar disorder? Researchers at USC, Stanford, and Johns Hopkins received a $4.5M BD² grant to study "retrosplenial switch cells"—a unique neuronal population that may control mood switching.

stories.title: How brain implants turn thoughts into speech
stories.summary: New brain-computer interfaces turn attempted speech into words and can speak them in a voice resembling the user’s own.

stories.title: The secret to slower aging may be hiding in your gut
stories.summary: The secret to aging more slowly may be hiding in your gut. Scientists discovered that certain gut bacteria are strongly linked to how quickly the body ages, with microbial differences accounting for about 15% of the variation in biological aging rates.

stories.title: Low testosterone may make sugar far more harmful to your liver
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that low testosterone and a high-fructose diet can work together to worsen fatty liver disease in mice. Unexpectedly, changes in gut bacteria appear to drive this harmful interaction, revealing a potential new target for preventing liver damage.

stories.title: Common drugs may help dangerous viruses spread through the body
stories.summary: A surprising discovery reveals that widely used anti-inflammatory drugs may unintentionally help dangerous viruses spread through the body.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising clue to why some brains resist Alzheimer’s
stories.summary: Why do some people stay mentally sharp even when their brains show signs of Alzheimer’s disease? Scientists in the Netherlands may have uncovered an important clue hidden in a rare group of immature brain cells.

stories.title: Mayo Clinic discovers new ways to fight the “zombie” cells that drive aging
stories.summary: Mayo Clinic scientists have uncovered surprising new insights into “zombie cells,” aging cells that linger in the body and contribute to inflammation and disease.

stories.title: The surprisingly simple exercise that could lower your blood pressure
stories.summary: A surprisingly simple exercise routine could help lower blood pressure without requiring daily workouts or expensive equipment.

stories.title: Exercise doesn't just strengthen your heart. It rewires it
stories.summary: Regular exercise does more than strengthen the heart. New research reveals that it actually reshapes the nerves controlling how the heart functions, and the changes are surprisingly different on the left and right sides of the body.

stories.title: Scientists reveal the hidden danger of missing blood pressure medication
stories.summary: Missing blood pressure medication could mean losing much of its protection against heart attacks and strokes, according to an analysis of more than 91,000 people.

stories.title: Low-dose aspirin linked to 70% lower dementia risk, but there's a catch
stories.summary: A common, inexpensive medication could hold an unexpected clue to preventing dementia. Researchers found that older adults with a specific genetic profile had a 70% lower relative risk of dementia when taking low-dose aspirin, even though previous studies found no overall protective effect.

stories.title: Popular cannabis sleep gummies may have a hidden dark side
stories.summary: A cannabis-derived ingredient commonly found in sleep gummies may be more habit-forming than previously thought, with new research showing that repeated exposure caused tolerance and withdrawal symptoms in mice.

stories.title: Mediterranean diet may boost tiny proteins that protect the heart and brain
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising new clue to why the Mediterranean diet is so good for the heart, brain, and healthy aging.

stories.title: Could lowering high blood pressure be as simple as stimulating your ear?
stories.summary: A small device that gently stimulates nerves through the ear could offer a new way to tackle stubborn high blood pressure. In a clinical trial of 63 patients already taking medication, the treatment proved safe, easy to use at home, and well tolerated.

stories.title: Glioblastoma breakthrough reveals how brain cancer cells become more aggressive
stories.summary: Scientists discovered that the thick, sticky fluid surrounding glioblastoma tumors can make brain cancer cells smaller, more flexible, and better at invading surrounding tissue.

stories.title: Personalised cancer vaccine expected to be approved next year
stories.summary: A bespoke vaccine that is tailored to target an individual's unique skin cancer reduced rates of recurrence or death in a late-stage trial, making an approval expected

stories.title: Breakthrough PTSD treatment achieves 68% remission rate in clinical trial
stories.summary: A newly FDA-cleared PTSD treatment uses personalized brain mapping and magnetic stimulation to target abnormal brain activity, with a clinical trial reporting a 52% reduction in symptoms and 68% remission.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising double benefit of exercise for Parkinson’s
stories.summary: A seven-year study found that people with Parkinson’s disease who were more physically active experienced slower declines in memory, thinking, and movement abilities.

stories.title: Sleep Habits May Indicate a Type of Depression, Researchers Say
stories.summary: Researchers say people with ‘circadian depression’ might benefit from therapies that help adjust the body’s clock.

stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden messaging system deep inside the brain
stories.summary: A tiny region deep within the brain has surprised scientists by revealing a remarkably sophisticated communication system.

stories.title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial
stories.summary: The scientists involved say the results could mark a turning point in cancer treatment, bringing personalised medicine a step closer.

stories.title: Give more people weight-loss jabs on the NHS, say MPs
stories.summary: Current plans for 6% of eligible patients to get Mounjaro by 2028 unambitious, say MPs.

stories.title: Millions take fish oil for brain health. A two-year study found no benefit
stories.summary: A surprising two-year clinical trial found that fish oil supplements successfully delivered omega-3s to the brain but failed to improve memory or protect against Alzheimer's-related brain shrinkage.

stories.title: Coffee calories have jumped nearly 40%. Sugar isn't the biggest culprit
stories.summary: Your morning coffee may be packing more calories than you realize, and sugar isn't the biggest reason. A study of 30,000 Americans found that non-dairy creamer has overtaken sugar and milk as the leading source of added coffee calories, helping drive a nearly 40% increase between 2003 and 2018.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising secret behind the human brain’s wrinkles
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered why common marmosets have unusually small, smooth brains despite starting development much like other primates. The secret lies in subtle changes to brain-building cells that slow neuron production, revealing new clues about how the large, folded human brain evolved.

stories.title: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
stories.summary: Researchers analyzing nearly 150,000 Reddit posts uncovered unexpected symptom reports linked by users to unapproved versions of retatrutide, including increased appetite, sleep disturbances, and elevated heart rates.

stories.title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study
stories.summary: Drugs will be tested simultaneously, which it's hoped will speed up the process of finding new treatments for this common type of dementia.

stories.title: Cholesterol may disrupt the brain’s cleaning system in Alzheimer’s disease
stories.summary: The glymphatic system flushes toxins out of the brain, but this seems to be disrupted in Alzheimer's disease, and cholesterol may be involved

stories.title: Astronauts’ hearts just passed a surprising test for Mars
stories.summary: A new study tracking 13 astronauts suggests that the human heart may be surprisingly well equipped for a journey to Mars, especially with regular exercise during spaceflight.

stories.title: Just 4 minutes a day can dramatically improve strength after 65
stories.summary: A new Penn State study suggests that just four minutes of daily strength training can significantly improve mobility and physical function in older adults.

stories.title: Scientists find 10 different diets linked to slower aging
stories.summary: A study by DZNE finds that healthy eating is associated with slower biological aging—and that there is more than one way to eat healthily.

stories.title: Inside Health
stories.summary: Experts warn poor at-home injecting techniques and new drugs mean new health risks.

stories.title: Scientists finally uncover why statins can cause muscle pain
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising reason why statins, the widely prescribed cholesterol-lowering drugs that help prevent heart attacks and strokes, can sometimes cause muscle pain, weakness, and even severe muscle damage.

stories.title: Your aging brain may be trading memory for something more valuable
stories.summary: The aging brain may be undergoing a remarkable transformation rather than simply losing its abilities, shifting its focus from remembering details to understanding the bigger picture.

stories.title: Scientists find a way to fight Alzheimer’s brain damage without removing toxic tau
stories.summary: Scientists have found a promising way to protect the brain from Alzheimer’s-related damage by blocking immune cells that contribute to the destruction of neurons.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising link between vitamin C and cancer survival
stories.summary: A surprising clinical trial suggests that taking vitamin C daily could improve survival in people with precancerous blood disorders and early-stage blood cancers.

stories.title: Why some people escape Alzheimer’s despite carrying a high-risk gene
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered why some people with a high genetic risk of Alzheimer’s remain mentally sharp into their 80s, uncovering a rare mutation that protects the brain from harmful protein buildup.

stories.title: Just 3,000 steps a day may help slow Alzheimer's, scientists find
stories.summary: Walking just 3,000 steps a day could help slow Alzheimer’s-related brain changes, according to new research. Scientists discovered that physical activity was linked to less buildup of harmful tau proteins and nearly half the cognitive and functional decline, even in people already showing early…

stories.title: Scientists win 2026 Nobel Prize for controlling brain cells with light
stories.summary: A discovery in tiny algae led to a Nobel Prize-winning breakthrough that allows scientists to switch brain cells on and off using light. The revolutionary technique has already helped researchers activate memories and is opening new possibilities for restoring vision and treating brain disorders.

stories.title: "Mind-blowing" Alzheimer’s breakthrough: Two hours of sleep restored without clearing brain plaques
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered an unexpected culprit behind sleep loss in Alzheimer’s disease: overactive immune cells in the brain. By temporarily removing these cells, researchers restored more than two hours of sleep per day in mice, revealing a promising new target for treatment.

stories.title: Is it true that … you need to take 10,000 steps a day to be healthy?
stories.summary: The fitness benchmark has surprisingly unscientific origins – yet it does contain more than a kernel of truth The idea that we need to walk 10,000 steps a day originated not in medical research but in a 1960s marketing campaign for a pedometer, says Jack McNamara, senior lecturer in clinical…

stories.title: Modern neuroscience is rediscovering a surprising idea freud had 130 years ago
stories.summary: Researchers have identified striking parallels between Sigmund Freud’s century-old theories and modern neuroscience, suggesting that the brain’s constant predictions shape how we experience reality.

stories.title: Scientists discover a natural compound that could protect the brain from too much salt
stories.summary: Eating too much salt may do more than raise blood pressure. It could also harm memory and social behavior. In a new study, Japanese researchers discovered that a soy-derived compound called LPC70 helped protect mice from several damaging effects of a high-salt diet.

stories.title: Eating blueberries every day may have a surprising effect on your mood
stories.summary: Eating blueberries every day could have surprising effects on mood, according to a small study that found greater reductions in depressive symptoms among older adults who consumed the fruit for three months.

stories.title: Scientists uncover 3 key brain pathways linked to lasting depression relief
stories.summary: Researchers have uncovered three brain pathways linked to lasting improvements in people receiving deep brain stimulation for severe, treatment-resistant depression.

stories.title: Scientists find a youth protein that helps aging brain cells act young again
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that a protein linked to youth helps protect the brain’s immune cells from age-related decline.

stories.title: New drug reverses severe fatty liver disease by repairing the gut
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that a potential new drug can reverse severe fatty liver disease in animal models by restoring gut health and blocking harmful substances from reaching the liver.

stories.title: Brain cells meant to protect us may be fueling cognitive decline
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising cause of age-related cognitive decline involving brain cells previously thought to be entirely beneficial.

stories.title: Scientists discover how deep sleep builds muscle, burns fat, and boosts the brain
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered a surprising two-way relationship between sleep and growth hormone, revealing how the brain carefully balances physical recovery with wakefulness.

stories.title: Yale scientists discover how stress changes the brain to make memories stronger
stories.summary: Yale scientists have uncovered how the stress hormone cortisol helps the brain turn emotional experiences into stronger, longer-lasting memories.

stories.title: Scientists discover how exercise reverses muscle aging
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden biological mechanism that helps explain how exercise can reverse some of the damage caused by muscle aging. The key is a gene called DEAF1, which becomes overactive with age and interferes with the muscles’ ability to clear damaged proteins and repair themselves.

stories.title: Mysterious brain activity under anesthesia challenges what we know about consciousness
stories.summary: Even under general anesthesia, the human brain can analyze language, recognize different types of words, and predict what comes next in a story, according to a surprising discovery by Baylor researchers.

stories.title: Rare study reveals a striking divide inside an Alzheimer’s patient’s brain
stories.summary: A rare examination of an Alzheimer’s patient’s brain revealed that regions cleared of amyloid plaques had remarkably little of the harmful tau buildup associated with memory loss, while neighboring areas showed extensive damage.

stories.title: Menopause is a biological transition that’s become a lucrative consumer business
stories.summary: While menopause media coverage helps to bust taboos, it also fosters a lucrative, social media and business-driven market that takes advantage of woman’s need for support.

stories.title: Strokes have nearly doubled among younger adults, and scientists aren't sure why
stories.summary: Strokes are becoming alarmingly common among younger adults, with rates nearly doubling among people ages 20 to 54 over nearly three decades.

stories.title: Ozempic and Wegovy linked to rare risk of sudden vision loss
stories.summary: Popular diabetes and weight loss drugs such as Ozempic and Wegovy have been linked to a slightly increased risk of a rare condition that can cause sudden, potentially permanent vision loss.

stories.title: A 47-year study reveals the age when your body starts losing strength
stories.summary: A 47-year study has uncovered a surprising turning point in physical aging: fitness and strength begin declining around age 35, even among people who exercise regularly.

stories.title: Cancer is rising in younger adults, and scientists can't fully explain why
stories.summary: A major study found that several cancers are rising faster among younger adults in England, even as smoking, diet, and other established risk factors have generally improved.

stories.title: Decade-long gym steroids study shows just what happens to men's hearts
stories.summary: One of the first long-term studies that followed weight-training middle-aged men for nearly a decade has found that consistent use of anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) leads to the thickening of the heart’s left ventricular wall, which increasingly reduces the organ's ability to function.

stories.title: Scientists reveal why some workout recovery tricks can backfire
stories.summary: Ice baths, massages, compression garments, and recovery supplements promise faster muscle recovery, but research suggests their benefits are often overstated, and some techniques may even undermine long-term gains.

stories.title: Scientists may have overlooked a hidden Alzheimer's culprit for decades
stories.summary: For decades, scientists have focused on amyloid beta as a major culprit behind Alzheimer’s disease, spending billions of dollars developing treatments that have often delivered disappointing results.

stories.title: Scientists discover how harmful “zombie cells” hide from the immune system
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered a protein that may help harmful aging cells hide from the immune system, allowing them to accumulate and fuel age-related health problems.

stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising paradox in how our cells age
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered that the body's cellular recycling system behaves very differently during aging than previously believed, with higher activity sometimes linked to worse physical health.

stories.title: The secret to handling stress better may start at breakfast
stories.summary: Your daily routine could have a bigger impact on your ability to handle stress than you realize. A Binghamton University study of approximately 400 college students found that eating breakfast regularly, exercising, sleeping well, and taking fish oil were associated with greater psychological…

stories.title: Scientists uncover a hidden map of the brain with 539 distinct regions
stories.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden layer of organization in the brain by creating the first detailed 3D map of its lipids, the fatty molecules essential for brain structure and communication.

stories.title: After 30 years, scientists finally have a drug for a deadly brain disease
stories.summary: The FDA has approved the first drug that directly targets Alexander disease, a devastating neurological disorder affecting fewer than one in a million people.

stories.title: Scientists find a hidden problem with endless smartphone scrolling
stories.summary: Excessive smartphone use may be taking a hidden toll on the brain and body, with heavy scrolling linked to poorer memory, reduced attention, disrupted sleep, and potential balance problems.

stories.title: Scarred blood vessels may be one clue to APOE4’s Alzheimer’s risk
stories.summary: Scientists know APOE4 raises Alzheimer’s risk. A surprising change in blood vessel cells may help explain how.

stories.title: Popular weight loss drugs linked to a surprising fingernail problem
stories.summary: Popular GLP-1 weight loss drugs, such as Ozempic and Wegovy, have been linked to unexpectedly high rates of nail detachment, hair loss, and scalp inflammation, with some problems occurring several times more frequently among users.

stories.title: Scientists find hidden driver of aging and a simple amino acid that fights memory loss in mice
stories.summary: Scientists discovered that declining levels of a protein called Menin may help drive aging, and restoring it in older mice reversed several age-related changes in just 30 days.

stories.title: Just 10 minutes of daily exercise could unlock deeper sleep
stories.summary: Getting better sleep might be as simple as moving a little more every day. Researchers at The University of Texas at Austin found that people who exercised more frequently experienced more deep, restorative sleep, which is essential for brain recovery, memory, and emotional well-being.

stories.title: The hidden math of Alzheimer's could point to new treatments
stories.summary: Mathematics may hold unexpected clues to understanding Alzheimer’s disease. Scientists have developed a model showing how common metals like copper and zinc may influence the buildup of proteins associated with the disease, while also exploring possible ways to stop the process.

stories.title: Eating olive oil before carbs has a surprising effect on blood sugar
stories.summary: A simple change in the order you eat your food could help prevent blood sugar spikes. Scientists discovered that giving mice olive oil before carbohydrates slowed digestion and activated a surprising combination of hormones and nerve signals that helped regulate blood sugar, even in mice with type…

stories.title: A surprisingly simple way to relieve knee arthritis pain without pills or surgery
stories.summary: A surprisingly simple change in how you walk could help relieve knee arthritis pain and even slow joint damage. In a year-long clinical trial, researchers found that adjusting the angle of a person's foot while walking reduced osteoarthritis pain by an amount comparable to medication, without…

stories.title: Scientists discover 5 hidden brain patterns behind depression
stories.summary: Depression may not be one biological condition, but several distinct patterns of brain activity hiding under the same diagnosis.

stories.title: Only one workout helped older adults lose fat and keep muscle
stories.summary: A six-month study suggests that high-intensity interval training (HIIT) may offer older adults a powerful advantage: losing body fat while keeping their muscle.

stories.title: Nearly 30,000 people tested quit-smoking methods. One stood out
stories.summary: Nicotine e-cigarettes appear to help more smokers quit than patches, gum, and several other common approaches, according to a major review of 80 clinical trials.

stories.title: Scientists tested 5 natural compounds on cancer cells. One stood out
stories.summary: Five natural compounds, including curcumin and berberine, were tested for their effects on cancer cells and healthy muscle cells. All disrupted cancer cell energy production and pushed many of the cells into a non-dividing state, with curcumin producing the strongest overall effect.

stories.title: FDA-approved epilepsy drug may help reverse osteoarthritis damage
stories.summary: Researchers at Yale have identified a promising new approach to osteoarthritis that could do more than simply ease pain. The epilepsy drug lacosamide appears to block a protein involved in both pain signaling and cartilage destruction, helping damaged joints shift back toward repair in preclinical…

stories.title: An experimental drug kills fat cells, rather than shrinking them
stories.summary: Participants in two small trials lost dangerous fat around their internal organs. This fat is linked to health issues like diabetes and heart problems.

stories.title: Just 7 days of strength training started shrinking fat cells in mice
stories.summary: Just seven strength-training sessions helped obese mice shrink visceral fat cells and reactivate molecular pathways involved in burning stored fat, despite no change in overall body weight.

stories.title: Scientists warn a popular vitamin D supplement may have a hidden downside
stories.summary: Not all vitamin D supplements are created equal, and new research suggests that one popular form may have an unexpected downside.

stories.title: Gene therapy and special goggles give some blind people limited sight
stories.summary: Optogenetics, recognized by the 2026 medicine Nobel, makes cells respond to light, including eye cells that normally relay signals to the brain.

stories.title: Drug target could block brain inflammation linked to Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s
stories.summary: Blocking a receptor called P2X7 significantly reduced inflammation in human brain tissue, revealing a potential new treatment strategy for neurological and psychiatric disorders.

stories.title: Goodbye joint replacements? Stanford scientists found a way to regrow cartilage and stop arthritis
stories.summary: Scientists have found a surprising way to regrow damaged knee cartilage by blocking a protein that becomes more abundant with age.

stories.title: Scientists say this simple habit could strengthen your marriage
stories.summary: Couples who exercise together report better communication, healthier conflict resolution, and lower marital stress than those who work out alone. Even something as simple as taking a walk together may create valuable opportunities to talk, listen, and feel more connected.

stories.title: A few drops of this Japanese tree oil may help you sleep more soundly
stories.summary: In a small study, sleeping near the scent of Hinoki root essential oil was linked to fewer nighttime awakenings, better morning alertness, and brain-wave changes associated with smoother sleep onset.

stories.title: Vagus Nerve Stimulation Could Help New Skills Stick
stories.summary: Stimulating the vagus nerve after practice helped mice develop stronger long-term motor learning, revealing a potentially important window when the brain is still locking in a new skill.

stories.title: Easing constipation: A 20-minute walk can get your gut moving almost immediately
stories.summary: Researchers found that just 20 minutes of comfortable walking can rapidly stimulate the gut. Within one to two minutes after exercise, bowel sounds became stronger, more frequent, and lasted longer, suggesting increased intestinal movement.

stories.title: Your gut bacteria may reveal how fast your brain is aging
stories.summary: A UCLA study links faster brain aging to specific gut bacteria and chemical byproducts, with older-looking brains also associated with poorer memory, focus, and mood.

stories.title: This common vitamin could help fight one of the deadliest brain cancers
stories.summary: High-dose vitamin B3 is showing intriguing early promise as an addition to standard glioblastoma treatment, with 82% of patients in a small trial remaining progression-free after six months.

stories.title: Vitamin D drug may help crack pancreatic cancer’s protective shield
stories.summary: A vitamin D analog may help break down pancreatic cancer’s protective defenses, potentially making tumors more vulnerable to chemotherapy and immune attack. A small clinical trial found encouraging responses, especially in patients whose tumors had high levels of the vitamin D receptor.

stories.title: Diet drinks work as well as water for weight loss, major trial finds
stories.summary: A two-year randomized clinical trial involving 493 adults with overweight or obesity found that diet soft drinks were essentially as effective as water for long-term weight loss and weight maintenance.

stories.title: Leucine does more than build muscle. It powers up your cells
stories.summary: The essential amino acid leucine can boost cellular energy production by protecting key proteins on mitochondria from being destroyed. The discovery reveals a new connection between nutrition and metabolism that could eventually lead to new approaches for metabolic disorders and cancer.

stories.title: Your gut may be making a molecule that raises Alzheimer’s risk
stories.summary: Scientists have linked a gut bacterial compound called ImP to greater Alzheimer’s risk, harmful brain protein buildup, and faster cognitive decline. The finding raises the possibility that reducing ImP in the blood could one day help slow or prevent dementia.

stories.title: Vitamin C linked to fewer deaths in blood disorder trial
stories.summary: Vitamin C may do more than support the immune system. In a phase 2 trial of people with precancerous or low risk blood cancers, daily vitamin C did not slow abnormal cell growth, but it was linked to favorable changes in inflammation and fewer serious complications.

stories.title: Cancer stem cells have an “energy addiction” scientists may be able to exploit
stories.summary: High-risk MDS stem cells appear to have an unexpected “energy addiction,” relying far more heavily than healthy blood-forming cells on a molecule called NAD. Disrupting this energy pathway selectively weakened the cancer-driving cells, revealing a potential new target for treatment.

stories.title: This diet may slow brain aging by 2.5 years
stories.summary: People who followed the MIND diet more closely showed slower brain shrinkage and less grey matter loss over time, with the strongest differences equivalent to about 2.5 years of delayed brain aging.

stories.title: Could quitting ultra-processed food boost your mental health?
stories.summary: People with depression who dramatically cut ultra-processed foods experienced notable improvements in their symptoms in a small preliminary study. Researchers suspect healthier eating may benefit the brain partly by reducing gut damage and chronic inflammation.

stories.title: Alzheimer’s risk gene APOE4 may have a reversible weakness
stories.summary: The Alzheimer’s risk gene APOE4 may actively damage brain blood vessels and sabotage the cellular systems that remove harmful proteins.

stories.title: Creatine may help build muscle even without exercise, researchers find
stories.summary: Creatine helped middle-aged adults gain muscle and strength even without a structured workout program in a new 12-week study. When combined with exercise and a calorie-reduced diet, it produced even greater strength gains while helping participants add lean tissue and lose fat.

stories.title: Brain scans reveal which disorders are linked to faster brain aging
stories.summary: A massive MRI study found that Alzheimer’s disease, mild cognitive impairment, psychiatric disorders, and addiction are associated with distinct patterns of accelerated brain aging.

stories.title: Scientists just discovered what coffee really does to your gut and brain
stories.summary: A new study suggests coffee may influence mood and brain function by changing the activity of microbes in the gut. Both caffeinated and decaf coffee were linked to lower stress, depression, and impulsivity, while also producing measurable changes in gut bacteria and metabolites.

stories.title: 160-million-year-old proteins show surprising power against superbugs
stories.summary: Scientists resurrected antimicrobial peptides from mammals that lived millions of years ago and found that some were more potent against drug-resistant bacteria than modern human versions.

stories.title: Resetting the body clock could help the brain recover after stroke
stories.summary: Strengthening the body’s natural daily rhythms helped mice recover after stroke by improving the brain’s waste-clearing system and reducing lingering inflammation.

stories.title: Scientists found a surprising driver of Alzheimer’s outside the brain
stories.summary: Scientists found that immune cells contributing to Alzheimer’s-related brain damage may be activated in lymph nodes outside the brain before traveling into the nervous system.

stories.title: Glucosamine, a popular joint supplement, linked to faster Alzheimer’s progression
stories.summary: A large health-record analysis found that glucosamine use was associated with a 25% higher likelihood of mild cognitive impairment progressing to dementia.

stories.title: Why rheumatoid arthritis pain may persist even when inflammation is under control
stories.summary: Pain and fatigue in rheumatoid arthritis can persist even after inflammation improves, with depression, poor sleep, obesity, smoking, and chronic pain potentially helping sustain symptoms.

stories.title: ‘It’s problematic’: concern as weight-loss jab maker sponsors Vogue World event
stories.summary: Critics say partnership between Mounjaro maker Eli Lilly and fashion giant suggests thinness is an aspiration The fifth iteration of Vogue World , overseen by Anna Wintour, took place in Milan on Tuesday night.

stories.title: Scientists say house cats could help unlock better cancer treatments for humans
stories.summary: Scientists have mapped the genetics of cat cancer on an unprecedented scale and found surprising similarities with tumors in humans. The findings could help bring precision cancer treatments to cats while also revealing new clues about how human cancers develop and respond to drugs.

stories.title: REM sleep paradox: Dreaming may drain the brain’s energy even as fuel supply rises
stories.summary: Scientists discovered a surprising energy paradox in the brain during REM sleep, the stage most closely associated with dreaming. Blood supply to the brain begins increasing even before REM starts, but neurons’ immediately available energy, measured as ATP, then drops.

stories.title: Scientists gave worms magnetic bacteria. They lived 43% longer
stories.summary: A magnet-producing bacterium extended the average lifespan of C. elegans worms by more than 43% while helping protect their neurological and intestinal health.

stories.title: Aging muscles may be losing strength for a reason scientists missed
stories.summary: A newly identified breakdown in communication between nerves and muscles could help explain why people lose strength as they age. Researchers were able to improve muscle strength in an animal model by targeting a key protein, raising hopes that some age-related weakness could eventually be treated.

stories.title: Breakthrough drug reverses skin aging and dramatically speeds healing
stories.summary: A topical drug that removes aging, damaged cells helped older mice heal skin wounds significantly faster. The treatment appeared to reactivate repair pathways involved in inflammation, collagen production, and new blood vessel growth.
